Episode 210. Memories of the Past - Murakan (1)
There had already been several painful choices.

Among them, what remained was the most horrifying choice, and Murakan had made up his mind. Today, he would stop Temar, and he too would be forgotten from this world, along with everything he had loved.

The spirit energy emanating from his double wings formed a massive storm. The ultimate secret technique of Murakan in his prime, the Advent of the True Darkness, engulfed everything in sight with darkness.
Temar managed to suppress his boiling rage.
Because the moment he succumbs to demonic rage, he could never beat Murakan, or the fact that he was already a monster, which he was totally oblivious of.
Temar's sword wasn't as sharp as when it was originally forged, and his will was tarnished by the manipulation of history and its side effects.

"No, you're the only one who will be erased from history. As always, I will protect my clan and the people. I will correct the distorted events, and destroy traitors like you and all the enemies. I am, the head of Runcandel."
Temar's eyes were shining vividly.
Runcandel's demonic sword secret technique
The Splitting of the Sun
Aura, magic power, and spirit energy wrapped around the spear. The spiral quickly seeped into the blade, blackening it before burning bright white.
The pinnacle of the sword finally reached by a human named Temar Runcandel.
As the blade began to move, the darkness formed by the Advent of the True Darkness receded. Light began to fill the place instead of darkness, as if murky water had turned clear.

If Temar had been in his prime, Murakan would never have tried to face the Splitting of the Sun head-on. It is a sword that could take his life in a single blow, even in his prime, if he could not evade it.
But the Splitting of the Sun displayed by the current Temar is merely half of what it should be.
The Soul Reaping he had been using all along was far more threatening. Murakan filled the wiped area of the Advent of the Dark with spirit energy again and charged towards Temar.
The shining sword and the black spirit energy formed into a massive blade were colliding.
Temar was certain that his sword would cut through the spirit energy and Murakan in one breath. It was just strange that Murakan didn't even consider avoiding his all-in attack.
Murakan would know it better than anyone else. How Solderet described this sword. Solderet said that the Splitting of the Sun was a sword that could kill even him if it touched him.
However, at the moment of collision, Temar had to face the Splitting of the Sun dissolving futilely in Murakan's spirit energy.
The aura, magic power, and spirit energy concentrated in the blade were unwinding powerlessly, as if a thread had been cut.
On the other hand, the giant black blade poured from Murakan's wings was undamaged at all. It was even more sharp and ferocious, attacking Temar more than before the collision.
Temar tried to dodge quickly by twisting his body, but Murakan's blade was faster. The blade passed by, cutting off Temar's left arm.
Thump!
Temar's left arm fell under the darkness of the True Dark Arrival. The arm disappeared, buried in the darkness, and Temar quickly raised his magic to freeze his wound.
He couldn't believe the result.
He couldn't accept the fact that a sword capable of even injuring Solderet was broken by Murakan. He couldn't understand what was lacking, what mistake had been made.
In that one moment when Temar's inner self wavered, Murakan was able to strike at his weakness and take his life.
Over the course of more than two thousand years, he had countless memories of harming others.
Countless memories of killing others, of leaving others crippled.
However, they were all enemies, or those who had antagonized him first. Murakan had never hurt a being he loved.
That's what made Murakan hesitate. The horrifying and unfamiliar sensation of having wounded a friend made his breathing become rapid, and his mind become foggy.
Dranax, Vyollo, Frey.
In fact, ever since he decided to kill them, the guilt that had built up was about to explode, causing his insides to churn.
[Temar, Temar.]
He couldn't bear to see himself failing to protect them, and even going so far as to take their lives.
Without realizing it, Murakan descended to look for Temar's left arm. The darkness of the Dark Arrival, which had always been a source of pride, felt unfamiliar and dirty for the first time.
Meanwhile, Temar was dealing with the backlash that had begun with the breaking of the Sun Splitter.
“Are you planning to belittle us more like this, Murakan? What are you doing in the middle of a fight?”
[That's not it.]
“Fight properly! Even if I lose all four limbs, I can still fight. Even if I lose my life to you today, I'll be reborn and come after you.”
Swoosh-!
Temar's strike cut off one of Murakan's wings. Murakan, without even thinking of regenerating with his energy, continued to think about Temar's left arm.
Despite his dire determination.

He didn't have the courage to kill Temar. The voices of the dead knights were constantly ringing in his ears. The voices filled with hatred, asking if he was going to brutally kill the head of the house with his own hands.
Then, Barisada cut next to Murakan's heart, and stabbed his abdomen and neck. Murakan couldn't even feel the pain.
He felt it would be better to die here himself. He wanted to end this nightmare. If he could end it with death, he felt he could give up life a thousand, ten thousand times over.
Just as he was on the verge of completely breaking down.
[No... Temar!]
Murakan was confronted by the sight of Temar transforming into a violet monster. The phantasmalization of historical manipulation was taking place.
Even demonization was spreading. Because of this, unlike the previous knights, Temar's facial features had not completely disappeared.
His grotesquely open mouth was full of irregular, sharp teeth, and his pupils were dark and empty.
The wildly swinging sword had none of the dignity of Genesis left, and now whenever Temar narrowed the distance, he bit into Murakan like a beast.

When the situation reached this point, Murakan's mind finally collapsed and he could not fight properly. He was just reflexively pushing Temar away, exerting all his strength to deny the monstrous figure he saw.
The heart wounded by the soul-cutting earlier was twisted. In the midst of fading, the eerie pain radiating from the heart occasionally made him feel reality.
It confirmed the sight of the contracted friend who had become a ghost.
Primitive violence of mindlessly scratching and biting each other continued. To call it a fight, Murakan was just struggling. Only Temar was viciously attacking Murakan.
Murakan was thinking.
It was not the first time he decided to kill Temar. Even the day when he went crazy with demonization, killed his allies, and hid in the tower of the black sea.
He thought he would have collapsed like now if he had gone to the end then. Then Orgal helped, but he thought he would have stopped eventually even if there was no such help.
It would have been the same for Sarah and Padler who went with him.
But he had to be different.
The guardian dragon, the being that protects the contractor.
Protecting is not just about life. When he is no longer himself, when he can't be turned back, letting him go was also part of protecting him.
Temar, weakened by the ghostification and demonization, couldn't even withstand Murakan's struggling. Even with Murakan's clumsily swinging forefoot, Temar screamed as his whole body was torn.
Temar's sharp fangs broke as they dug into Murakan's scales, and the right arm holding the Barisada couldn't overcome the recoil and broke on its own.
Temar was falling apart.
Finally, Murakan stared at him straight on with wide-open eyes. Despite his contorted body, he stared at Temar, who kept rushing at him.

[Do you hate me that much, are you so wronged that you're going crazy? Me too, Temar. I can't forgive myself, I'm so frustrated with the past days of intense fighting that I feel like my head will explode.]
Now was the time to protect Temar.
The gray landscape of the destroyed moon was revealed as the spirit that had accomplished the true Dark Advent returned to Murakan in an instant.
Murakan transformed into a human and descended to the ground. Temar staggered toward Murakan.
Before protecting him, Murakan wanted to confirm one last thing. Just once, he wanted to grope for hope.
Just as he and his comrades cherished him more than their own lives.
Even though Temar was being eroded by historical manipulation and devilishness, he might still somewhere, somewhere in that monstrous figure, cherish his friends and comrades.
Murakan didn't hesitate anymore.
He stood still like a tree, waiting for him to reach him with his staggering steps. Prepared to have his heart pierced, to offer his heart.
Just for a moment, he wished him to return to the person he and his comrades knew. He wanted to see that figure, even if it was just for a few seconds.
Everything couldn't just be forgotten and disappear like this. No matter how cruel the manipulation of history, all those times couldn't just disappear.
Plodding, plodding.
Thunk...
In the end, Temar stabbed Murakan's undefended heart. Ignoring the Barisada embedded in his chest, Murakan met Temar's gaze.
"Is it over now? Even after piercing my heart, you really can't regain your senses even for a moment?"
If Temar showed no signs of suffering.
Now he was to take his breath and collapse, then everything would be over. Even with a destroyed heart, he could kill the monstrous Temar easily.
There was no answer for a while.
But finally, Murakan could face the sight of Temar's body wrapped in violet and his grotesquely transformed face returning to its old self.
With trembling lips, Temar barely moved and managed to reply to Murakan.
"Murakan, you should have killed me... and prepared for the future. You should have saved more of our comrades, people, even one person. What meaning does my life have now that you're doing this...!"
"Ah... this bastard finally blabbering something like you would. I'm glad, eh. I'm so glad I could cry."

"I'll turn back into a monster soon, Murakan. Even Solderet can't stop it. So don't make such a reckless choice again, protect the family... the future. We can't all be forgotten like this. It all can't disappear. Someone has to remain. I'm sorry. I'm sorry, Murakan."
Soon, Murakan had no choice but to collapse. He could hear the sound of his shattered heart rattling in his chest.
As his consciousness faded, Murakan watched Temar's retreating figure.
Before Temar lost his reason, before he went mad again and killed the injured Murakan, he was desperately trying to get out of sight.
That was the last of Murakan and Temar.
